questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Give reasons for the rise of Dr E.M.L. Endeley as Premier of Southern Cameroons.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dr Emmanuel Mbella Lifafa Endeley, a medical doctor, rose from labour and pressure-group leader to Leader of Government Business (after 1954) and Premier (late 1950s) of the Southern Cameroons. Any seven reasons are accepted.

1. *Education and personality.* As a medical doctor he was respected and could negotiate with the British.
2. *Early leadership of pressure groups.* He founded the Cameroons Development Corporation Workers' Union (1947) and was a leading figure of the Cameroons National Federation, which gave him a following among plantation workers.
3. *Founding of the KNC (1951).* He led the first major party of the Southern Cameroons, formed from the merger of the Cameroons Youth League and the Cameroons National Federation, and it won the early elections.
4. *Leadership in the Eastern Region crisis (1953).* He led the walk-out of the elected members and the Mamfe Conference, and was seen as the champion of a separate Southern Cameroons.
5. *Quasi-federal status of 1954.* The status he obtained, with its own House of Assembly at Buea, made him head of government.
6. *Support of the British authorities* and of chiefs and the educated class, who preferred a gradual evolution with Nigeria.
7. *Party organisation and election victories* in 1954 and 1957, in which the KNC won the largest number of seats.
8. *Strong support in the coastal south,* his home area, where his party had a solid base.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) State the factors that favoured the rise of Foncha to the post of Premier in Southern Cameroons by 1959.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
John Ngu Foncha, a former teacher from Nkwen near Bamenda, became Premier after the elections of January 1959. Any seven factors are accepted.

1. *Creation of the KNDP (1955).* He and A. N. Jua left the KNC and formed a new party with a clear programme.
2. *Reunification platform.* He promised to end the control of Nigeria and to reunify the Cameroons, which attracted voters who feared Nigerian domination.
3. *Support of the Grassfields.* The people of Bamenda and the north-west, who felt neglected by the southern leaders and by Nigerian officials, gave him their votes.
4. *Weakening of Endeley's party.* Dissatisfaction with Endeley's closeness to Nigeria, with party splits and with his policy on land and plantation workers cost his party votes.
5. *Grassroots campaigning.* Foncha toured villages, spoke in simple language, and presented himself as a humble man of the people.
6. *Support of other leaders and groups* such as S. T. Muna, A. N. Jua, chiefs, traders and women's groups in the grasslands.
7. *International context.* The independence of Ghana (1957), the coming independence of French Cameroon and Nigeria, and United Nations attention to the trust territory favoured a leader who spoke of independence.
8. *Election victory of 1959.* The KNDP won a narrow majority of the seats in the House of Assembly and Foncha became Premier.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) What were the main achievements of J.N Foncha as Premier during the period 1959 to 1961?

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Between 1959 and 1961 J. N. Foncha's main achievements were (any six):

1. *He kept the demand for reunification before the United Nations* and secured the plebiscite of 11 February 1961, in which the Southern Cameroons voted to join the Republic of Cameroon.
2. *He won the plebiscite campaign* for reunification, with the KNDP campaigning on the programme of independence by joining the Republic.
3. *He negotiated with the leaders of the Republic.* He met President Ahidjo and prepared for the Foumban talks, where a federal constitution was agreed (July 1961).
4. *He organised the All Party Conference at Bamenda (June 1961)* to agree on a common Southern Cameroons position before Foumban.
5. *He led the Southern Cameroons peacefully to union* on 1 October 1961, with no violence during the transition.
6. *He continued administration and development* in the territory (schools, roads, health services), within the limits of the small budget, and prepared civil servants for self-government.
7. *He became Prime Minister of West Cameroon and Vice-President of the Federal Republic* (1961), thus giving the Southern Cameroons a place in the new state.
